title: Quiet Start: Compact Onboarding Checklist & Skill-Pairing Protocol (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a "quiet start" approach to onboarding engineers and product-adjacent roles: reduce cognitive load in weeks 0–4, prioritize psychological safety, and create a repeatable skill-pairing protocol so new hires contribute safely and learn quickly. Use as a manager + people ops playbook and adapt per role.

Scope and assumptions:
- Intended for IC hires (I-1 through P-4) across eng, data, and product teams.
- Assumes access to base infra, laptop, and network is provisioned by day 0. If not, escalate via SRE onboarding channel.
- This is a compact, lower-noise alternative to typical high-contact bootcamps; it trades rapid exposure for calmer, deeper ramping when role or team bandwidth is limited.

Principles:
1) Psychological safety first — early checkpoints focus on questions vs. deliverables.
2) Low-risk contributions — choose first tasks that are visible but reversible (docs, tests, small infra fixes).
3) Structured pairing — every new hire has a 1:1 pairing schedule with two buddies: a technical buddy and a product/context buddy.
4) Asynchronous-first communication — default to written artifacts, recorded walkthroughs, and short demos.
5) Measurable ramp signals — define 3 simple signals to judge progress and adjust schedule.

Quick start checklist (manager + people ops responsibilities):
- 14 days before start: confirm role-specific first-week repo, 1–2 low-risk starter tickets, and pairing buddies assigned. Create a short "starter map" doc (1 page) that points to the top 5 resources.
- 7 days before: schedule day 0 welcome + security briefing, calendar invites for pairing blocks (30–60m) for week 1.
- Day 0 (Quiet Day):
  - Welcome email with 1-line objectives for Week 1 and links to starter map.
  - Ship laptop + credentials checklist verified.
  - Schedule a 20-minute non-technical intro with manager to cover expectations and psychological-safety norms.
  - Ask new hire to set 3 personal ramp goals (skills they want to practice) and share in their onboarding doc.
- Days 1–3 (Orientation, low pressure):
  - Day 1: 45m team intro + culture norms (recorded). No heavy ramping.
  - Day 2: Pairing with context buddy (30m) — product background, roadmap, team priorities.
  - Day 3: Pairing with tech buddy (30–60m) — repo walkthrough, dev environment boot, local tests.
  - Assign 1 small starter task: documentation improvement, test flake fix, or minor config change. Aim for a 1–2 hour ship.
- Days 4–7 (Small wins & feedback):
  - Daily 30-minute sync with manager or buddy to surface blockers. Keep these short and supportive.
  - Add a second starter ticket that introduces a bit more context (e.g., add telemetry to an existing endpoint).
  - End of week: asynchronous reflection doc from the new hire — what felt confusing, what helped.
- Week 2 (Confidence building):
  - Increase pairing cadence to 2x/week. Introduce the new hire to the oncall / reliability playbook at a high level (read-only).
  - Assign a reversible, ownerless task that requires reading 2–3 PRs and making a small improvement.
  - Manager runs a 30-minute calibration to revisit goals and remove blockers.
- Weeks 3–4 (Ownership & visibility):
  - New hire takes primary ownership of a small area: triage stream, doc set, or test suite.
  - Run a 1-hour demo: new hire presents their starter work and learning. Celebrate small wins.
  - End-of-30-day check: manager + new hire + buddy retrospective (30–45m). Capture evidence for hiring rubric alignment.

Skill-Pairing Protocol (repeatable template):
- Pairing roles:
  - Technical Buddy (TB): deep codebase knowledge; responsible for dev environment boot, code review guidance, and first PR pairing.
  - Context Buddy (CB): product/infra context, customer impact, and team-goals translator.

- Pairing cadence and format:
  - Week 1: TB 3x30m, CB 2x30m (mix of synchronous and recorded walkthroughs).
  - Week 2: TB 2x45m, CB 1x45m.
  - Weeks 3–4: 1x/week pairing for focused deep work.

- Session structure (30–45m):
  - 5m: quick check-in + micro-goal.
  - 20–30m: walk through task/code/readme and work together. Use shared screen and take notes in onboarding doc.
  - 5–10m: capture 2 action items and next steps. TB/CB should add a one-liner to the new hire's onboarding doc about what success looks like for the next pairing.

Starter task selection heuristics (for people managers):
- Must be reversible in <4 hours if bad.
- Should require reading but not heavy domain modeling.
- Adds observable value (fixes a test, improves docs, adds telemetry).
- Avoid core-data-path write workflows until Week 4 unless paired.

Manager checklist (first 30 days):
- Day 0: 20m psychological-safety conversation; set expectations on communication norms.
- Week 1: 3x short check-ins (15–30m).
- Week 2: 1x 30m calibration + adjust workload.
- End of Week 2: fill in two ramp signals and an activation projection.
- End of Week 4: 45–60m review meeting; update hire evidence to reflect rubric categories (technical skills, communication, ownership).

Ramp signals (pick up to 3, measured qualitatively):
- Can independently set up dev environment and run test suite (yes/no).
- Ships a small PR with tests and receives an approving review without heavy rework.
- Can explain the team’s primary product flow in 5 slides or less.

Interview evidence tie-in (how to convert onboarding notes into hiring signals):
- Map starter tasks to interview competencies: e.g., documentation PR => "clarity & domain translation"; telemetry addition => "observability and debugging"; test flake fix => "engineering craftsmanship".
- Capture 2–3 concrete artifacts after 30 days (links to PRs, onboarding doc reflections, demo recording) and attach to hiring record for future calibration.

Common failure modes & mitigations:
- Over-scheduling: reduce calendar invites and prefer asynchronous artifacts.
- Noisy ramp: aim for 60% asynchronous learning materials in week 1.
- Pairing mismatch: rotate buddies after Week 2 if chemistry or signal isn't working.
- Invisible blockers: weekly anonymous pulse check for new hires to surface issues safely.

Templates (copy into new hire's onboarding doc):
- 1-line Week-1 Objective: "Set up local dev, ship one small PR, and learn the team's top 3 repos."
- Starter map header: top 5 links (README, runbook, team-notes, first-issue, product-spec).
- Reflection prompt (end of week 1): "1) What was unclear? 2) What helped most? 3) One tiny change that would improve onboarding for next hire."

Activation metrics (for people ops to monitor across hires):
- Percentage of hires who shipped a starter PR within 14 days.
- Median time to first successful paired review.
- Satisfaction pulse score at day 7 and day 30 (1–5).

Next steps and open questions (WIP):
- Create a short recorded "quiet start" orientation that managers can reuse.
- Decide whether certain roles (e.g., security, infra) should have modified pairing cadence.
- Build a lightweight dashboard that tracks the three ramp signals per hire.

Notes to self / discussion points for people ops sync: 
- Consider integrating a template into the candidate offer packet so new hires know quiet-start expectations pre-first-day.
- Sync with SRE to create a "day 0 readiness" checklist that people ops can consume programmatically.

References and links:
- Onboarding checklist inspiration: internal "starter-map" repo and Confluence onboarding hub (linked above).
- Suggested reading: "Make Work Human" section on psychological safety and early autonomy.
